## 📚 Core Content

### [Concept 1 Title]

**[Explain the concept in plain language. Use simple analogies first, then introduce the technical term. Every code example below should have annotated comments explaining what each line does.]**

```c
#include <stdio.h>   // Include the standard input/output library
                      // This gives us access to printf()

int main(void)        // Every C program starts here
{
    // --- [Concept 1 demonstrated] ---
    
    // [Brief comment explaining the code below]
    int example = 42; // Declare an integer variable named 'example'
                      // and assign it the value 42
    
    printf("%d\n", example);  // Print the value of 'example' to the screen
                              // %d is a format specifier for integers
    
    return 0; // Signal that the program finished successfully
}
```

**[Explain what happens step by step when this code runs.]**

## 💡 Common Pitfalls

- ❌ **[Pitfall 1]** — *[Why it's wrong and what to do instead]*
  ```c
  // WRONG:
  int x = 10;
  printf(x);  // Wrong! printf needs a format string
  
  // RIGHT:
  int x = 10;
  printf("%d\n", x);  // Correct: format string matches variable type
  ```

> **[Explicitly connect this section's programming concept to the learner's existing knowledge. Use International Relations, diplomacy, organizational behavior, or everyday life.]**

> "When you study how the UN Security Council operates, you learn that there are rules about who can speak, when they can speak, and what happens after they speak. You're already a systems thinker. Now you're learning a new system."
